newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: KIWI STOWAWAYS APPEAR IN AUCKLAND COURT
The 18-year-old New Zealand twins who survived a three-week sea and bush ordeal in far North Queensland have appeared in an Auckland court following their deportation from Australia.
The two entered no plea to charges including theft and drink driving and were remanded in custody.
The charges relate to offences allegedly committed in New Zealand before they stowed away on a Malaysian containership in February.
In court, Joanne and Sarah Ingham were still wearing the same clothes they had on when they jumped ship off Cape York three weeks ago.
RUDDOCK SAYS HANSON'S ASIAN IMMIGRATION CLAIMS IGNORANT
Immigration Minister Philip Ruddock has dismissed as alarmist nonsense, Pauline Hanson's claims that Asian born Australians will make up more than half the population in 50-years.
On ABC Television last night, Ms Hanson also claimed Asian immigration is being covered up, because many Asians enter Australia through New Zealand but don't show up in statistics.
Mr Ruddock says Ms Hanson's statements are abysmally ignorant.
He says the Asian born population in 30 years will be seven-point-five per-cent, with immigration programs the same as they are now.
Mr Ruddock says it's alarmist and unhelpful to any constructive debate to suggest otherwise, particularly without sourcing the claim.
GUN CONTROL UNDER HANSON "FRIGHTFUL"-CROOK
The President of Gun Control Australia says if Pauline Hanson's One Nation party takes on her views on gun control, Australia's future looks frightful.
John Crook says Miss Hanson's book indicates a firearms policy advocating the proliferation of guns and easy civilian access to military style weapons.
Mr Crook says Pauline Hanson is one of Australia's most dangerous politicians, with one of the most irresponsible gun policies ever devised by a Member of Parliament.
GOVT CONDEMNED FOR NOT HOLDING PUBLIC INQUIRY
Fairfax Chairman, Sir Laurence Street, has condemned the Federal Government for not holding a public inquiry into media ownership laws.
The former judge has also criticised any plans to break-up Fairfax, which he says would lead to print media domination to the News Corporation.
There's speculation the Federal Government favours a relaxation of cross-media ownership rules, which would allow Kerry Packer to buy Fairfax if he sold the Australian Financial Review.
Sir Laurence says a public inquiry into media rules is needed.
HOLMES-A-COURT SAY HANSON DAMAGING HER BUSINESS IN ASIA
Australian businesswoman, Janet Holmes-a-Court says many of her three-thousand Asian employees are concerned and embarrassed by comments made federal independent M-P Pauline Hanson.
Mrs Holmes-a-Court has told ABC radio that many of her Asian staff have children studying in Australia and have expressed concern about continuing that practice.
She says while she's glad the Prime Minister's spoken out against Ms Hanson's views, she believes he should have done it a lot sooner.
SHAKE UP OF SUICIDE PREVENTION POLICIES
Health policy makers are being urged to consider masculinity a risk factor in youth suicide.. as part of call for a radical shake-up of suicide prevention policies.
A men's health educator has told a trauma and grief conference in Sydney, current programs haven't been effective in reducing the alarming rates of male youth suicide.
Norman Dean Radican from the Royal North Shore Hospital in Sydney, says programs need to focus more on the causes of suicide.
